🔻 Iranian envoy attends Caspian Sea Littoral States meeting

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Kazem Gharibabadi, Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, has attended the meeting of the Working Group of Senior Officials of the Caspian Sea littoral states in Avaza, Turkmenistan.

The event was held with the presence of the special representatives of these countries for Caspian affairs in Avaza, Turkmenistan.
​
The participants reviewed the latest developments and various dimensions of the phenomenon of the declining water level of the Caspian Sea and its consequences.
​
They also stressed strengthening five-party cooperation to identify the causes of this phenomenon and counter its effects and consequences.
​
One of the most important topics examined was the proposal to establish a Commission of Caspian Littoral States to address issues related to the declining water level of the Caspian Sea.
​
The commission will be formed with the presence of senior officials of the littoral states and will place on its agenda the continuous examination of the dimensions and consequences of the declining Caspian water level and ways to counter it.
​
The outcomes of the Senior Officials Working Group meeting will be submitted for final approval as a decision at the special and extraordinary summit of Caspian littoral state leaders, convened on Friday in Avaza, Turkmenistan, to address Caspian environmental issues.

💬 Sanctions, threats failed to halt Iran’s nuclear health industry: Eslami

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) Mohammad Eslami said sanctions, threats and attacks against the country’s nuclear industry have failed to halt its progress in the field of health, stressing that Iran has maintained its advances at the frontiers of science.

Speaking at the inauguration of the country’s first university-based center for the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer on Thursday, Eslami said the AEOI considers health and food security a strategic responsibility for the country’s development.
​
“We take pride in being able to continue the path of progress despite all the pressures, sanctions, threats and attacks against the country’s nuclear industry,” he said.
​
Eslami added that alongside such pressures, Iran has also faced what he described as false allegations and claims against the country.
​
“Despite these circumstances, our colleagues have been able to carry out their mission successfully and preserve the country’s movement at the frontiers of science,” he said.
​
Eslami said Iran has expanded its radiopharmaceutical portfolio in line with leading countries, noting that around 78 products are currently being produced and supplied continuously under contracts with the Food and Drug Administration.
​
More than 20 additional products are also at the research stage, he said, adding that they would be added to the portfolio after completing clinical procedures and meeting Health Ministry requirements.
​
The AEOI chief also highlighted Iran’s achievements in alpha-emitting radiopharmaceuticals, saying the country was among the first to introduce such medicines into medical treatment.
​
He said Iran’s nuclear industry has been able to compete with the United States in the field of alpha-emitting medicines despite the threats facing the country.
